html:
The Malayan Emergency was a guerrilla war from 1948 to 1960 between the Malayan Communist Party, led by Chin Peng, and British and Malayan forces. It began with the killing of three European planters near Sungai Siput, in Perak.

Most guerrillas were Chinese, many of them former fighters against Japan. Under the Briggs Plan the British moved about half a million Chinese rural squatters into guarded New Villages to cut the guerrillas off from food.

General Gerald Templer pressed a campaign to win hearts and minds, and promises of independence took away the rebels' cause. The insurgency faded by the late 1950s. It became a model, often misread, for later counter-insurgency, including in the Vietnam War. See Cold War.
